title: Wonderful Life
summary: Casting George Bailey for a modern transposition of "It's a Wonderful Life", using two original AI performers, directed audition readings, and a repeatable test method.
logline: Two invented actors. One difficult role in the holiday classic "It's a Wonderful Life". A casting process built to find out which one can nail it.
description: My agentic casting director, Eva, designed two fictional performers from scratch, generated their casting headshots, and wrote a director's audition packet that tests each man on the same two scenes: Potter's offer, and the night George breaks his children's models. The goal is to judge performance, not just a pretty frame.
castNote: Both performers are original fictional designs, not likenesses of real people. Their headshots are candidate references at age 40, and neither is locked yet.

performers.name: Daniel Reyes
performers.alt: Casting headshot of Daniel Reyes, an AI-generated fictional performer. A man around 40 with warm medium-brown skin, short thick black hair with silver at the temples, heavy dark brows, and dark brown eyes. He is clean-shaven, with a faint closed-mouth smile that creases one cheek more deeply, and he looks straight at the camera. He wears a heather grey crew-neck T-shirt against a plain warm grey backdrop in soft, even light.
performers.desc: Compact and broad-chested, quick and magnetic. A credit union director who could have been a successful entrepreneur.
performers.objective: Wants the world to acknowledge his value.
performers.voice: Middle-low pitch, forward resonance, quick conversational emphasis.
performers.prompt: Photorealistic casting headshot, 85mm at eye level, soft daylight, warm grey backdrop, apparent age exactly 40. Warm medium-brown skin, close-set dark eyes, slightly bent nose, square jaw, silver starting at the temples, one deeper smile crease. Unretouched, a unique invented person.

concept.headline: The man who could have made money
concept.want: He wants the world to acknowledge his value.
concept.playingAge: Anchor at 40, with an apparent present-day range of 37–42; distinct younger adult states.
concept.physical: Latino; 5 feet 10 inches, compact and broad through the chest. Warm medium-brown skin, close-set dark eyes, strong brows, a slightly bent nose, broad mouth, and substantial jaw. Thick black hair, silver beginning at the temples; one cheek creases more deeply when he smiles.
concept.interpretation: This George could sell, negotiate, raise capital, and compete with Sam. His frustration comes from knowing he possesses commercially valuable abilities and repeatedly using them where the financial return is smallest.
concept.presence: Immediate engagement. He makes eye contact, remembers your problem, and starts solving it before you finish explaining.
concept.strengths: Persuasive rhythm, quick status changes, pleasure in a successful negotiation. At Potter’s offer, his breath releases and he settles comfortably into the chair for the first time.
concept.emotionalStrength: He restores dignity by treating someone’s difficulty as solvable.
concept.vulnerability: He needs recognition more than he admits. Potter’s acknowledgment reaches him before the salary does.
concept.contradiction: A convincing winner who privately feels overtaken by everyone he grew up with.
concept.whyHeWorks: The $310,000 offer becomes painfully credible. His rejection costs him a future the audience has already seen him inhabit.
concept.risk: His fluency could make the credit union scenes feel too easy. We need moments when persuasion fails and he must pay personally.
concept.costume: Carefully maintained, moderately priced suits; repaired dress shoes; open collar after hours. Precise haircut, clean-shaven face, wedding ring polished by habitual turning.
concept.effect: The conflict centers on recognition and economic worth. Mary must be someone whose judgment matters enough to puncture his practiced confidence.

performers.name: Adrian Shaw
performers.alt: Casting headshot of Adrian Shaw, an AI-generated fictional performer. A lean man around 40 with light olive skin, high cheekbones, and a narrow, angular jaw with light stubble. His dark hair is tousled and swept back, with a few grey strands at the temples. He has brown almond-shaped eyes under straight dark brows and a neutral, closed-mouth expression. He wears a heather grey crew-neck sweater against a plain grey backdrop in soft, even light.
performers.desc: Lean, with a long neck and contained restless intelligence. A man who expected to become an architect.
performers.objective: Wants a life that feels commensurate with his promise.
performers.voice: Middle pitch, precise consonants, compressed phrase endings when holding back.
performers.prompt: Photorealistic casting headshot, 85mm at eye level, soft daylight, warm grey backdrop, apparent age exactly 40. Light olive skin, high cheekbones, almond eyes under straight brows, subtly uneven angular jaw, stubborn crown, sparse silver at the temples. Attractive but ordinary, never model-perfect.

concept.headline: The man who cannot bear being ordinary
concept.want: He wants a life that feels commensurate with his promise.
concept.playingAge: Anchor at 40; apparent range 36–41, with fatigue and age carried through texture and behavior.
concept.physical: Mixed East Asian and white; 6 feet 0 inches, lean, long-necked, upright until exhausted. Light olive skin, high cheekbones, dark almond-shaped eyes beneath straight brows, a long nose with a rounded tip, defined lips, and a subtly uneven jaw. Dense straight black hair with a stubborn crown and sparse temple grey.
concept.interpretation: George grew up certain that his speed and imagination were taking him somewhere. He remains curious and verbally expansive, but wants each problem to yield to an elegant solution. Small compromises accumulate as private humiliations.
concept.presence: Focused, attractive, slightly demanding. He listens intensely, then answers too soon because he believes he already understands.
concept.strengths: Thought visible before speech, brittle excitement, emotional exposure after failed control. At Potter’s handshake, the first refusal escapes softly; he studies Potter’s face as though surprised by what he himself has said.
concept.emotionalStrength: He can imagine possibilities that other people have stopped allowing themselves.
concept.vulnerability: He fears he has mistaken potential for achievement.
concept.contradiction: A composed exterior containing an increasingly frantic need to prove his life has amounted to something.
concept.whyHeWorks: Pottersville strips away his explanations. At the library, Mary’s complete lack of recognition defeats the man who has always relied on making himself understood.
concept.risk: He could become aloof. Establish bodily pleasure early: delighted dancing, ridiculous travel enthusiasm, unguarded attraction, laughter that briefly ruins his composure.
concept.costume: An older fitted blazer, plain shirts carefully ironed, narrow wool trousers, repeatedly resoled shoes. Grooming is a small area he can still control.
concept.effect: The story becomes particularly intimate about shame. The final look at Mary is his acceptance that he can belong to a life he cannot completely explain.

tests.title: Potter's offer
tests.setting: George at 34, a glass conference room in daylight. Potter is an off-camera reader; only his hand enters the frame.
tests.question: Does George accept in his head before the handshake, and can his first refusal come before he can explain it?

readings.objective: Let this man finally acknowledge what I am worth.
beats: Reads the salary twice. A held breath releases. His shoulders settle before the smile arrives.
Enjoys the offer openly. The near-laugh is involuntary; for a moment he speaks as Potter's equal.
Asks about Bailey as a practical detail, not a trap. Starts to answer, swallows it, asks for a day.
Takes the hand with ordinary confidence. The smile drains while contact holds. The first no surprises him.
The refusals gather speed before conviction catches up.
readings.watch: Pleasure at being valued, without turning smug. It fails if he's suspicious of Potter from the start.

readings.objective: Let this offer reopen the future I thought was gone.
beats: Reads the figure and goes still for one beat. His eyes lift toward the view, then return.
At the mention of travel his attention drifts; he's imagining movement. Real delight, not calculation.
The question about Bailey comes fast, hoping for a solution. The request to talk to Mary is sincere.
Takes the hand already anticipating the next step. The first no escapes him.
Holds the hand a fraction too long. The refusals tumble over each other.
readings.watch: Pleasure has to reach his body. It fails if the offer stays intellectual or the handshake plays as horror.

tests.title: The models
tests.setting: George at 40 on Christmas Eve, just after a hard phone call. A warm living room, one static take, the children off camera.
tests.question: Can his anger become frightening, and can he see its cost in his children's faces without asking us to forgive him?

readings.objective: Make the demands stop for one moment.
beats: Turns toward the piano too quickly. The second command is far louder than the room needs.
Raises the newel knob, catches himself late, and sets it down with too much care.
Clears the shelf of models in one fast sweep, a movement his practical body rarely allows.
Turns back as if to speak, sees a child's face, and finds nothing to say.
Takes his coat without meeting Mary's eyes. His apology runs out of breath. He leaves.
readings.watch: The capable man becomes someone whose next move is uncertain. No self-pity, no rueful charm.

readings.objective: Stop the room from exposing the distance between my life and the life I imagined.
beats: Tries to hold still through the piano. His breath shortens, then the command breaks out at Janie.
Lifts the knob on an ugly impulse, sees what's in his hand, and sets it down. No clean self-control.
His eyes find the tower for less than a second. Then the whole shelf goes, with sudden force.
Watches a fragment settle, looks up, and meets the children's silence. His jaw loosens.
Attempts a precise apology and can't sustain it. His voice thins on Janie's name. He leaves.
readings.watch: The danger stays immediate, never tastefully sad. Shame arrives only after the damage.
